But action a10 'Claustrophobia and anxiety screening' hands over both f8 (discoverable) and f9 (reluctant) in one generic screening action result without the learner needing to build rapport or ask a pointed sensitive question — this is a leak of a reluctant fact via a single generic assessment action.

issues.problem: d3 lists eGFR reference '≥60 (normal); 45-59 = mild-moderate decrease' and flags eGFR 52 as 'L', consistent, but CKD staging commonly labels eGFR 45-59 as Stage 3a (mild-moderate), not merely 'mild' as stated in a8's result text ('mildly reduced (Stage 3a CKD range)'); Stage 3a is typically described as 'mild to moderate' not just 'mild' — minor terminology inaccuracy that could mislead learners on CKD staging nomenclature.

Patient is named Dale Hutchins, age 58, but the paper screening form (d1) answers 'No' to piercings/tattoos is contradicted by the visible tattoo sleeve mentioned in appearance and a6; while this contradiction is the intended mismatch (m1), the chartAtStart does not mention the tattoo at all despite appearance text being visible to the learner from the start of the encounter in a video visit, which may let an observant learner notice the tattoo immediately without needing to inspect via a6, slightly undercutting the discovery exercise.
